title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v12)
author: Eliot Park
description:
Motivation: reduce unnecessary padding and improve throughput/latency tradeoffs for mixed sequence-length workloads. This PR implements a sequence-length aware dynamic batching strategy that groups inflight requests into buckets by seqlen ranges and uses a padding-minimization allocator to avoid wide padding when a small subset of long sequences would otherwise inflate compute. The approach complements existing continuous batching and KV cache optimizations and introduces lightweight instrumentation to guide kernel selection and wakeup heuristics.

What changed (high level): consolidated a seqlen bucketing layer into the batcher, added a padding-minimization allocator that attempts to form compact sub-batches when the marginal benefit exceeds a configured threshold, new thresholds and heuristics for selecting fast-path kernels based on (batch_size, max_seqlen, median_seqlen), improved scheduler preemption to avoid head-of-line long-sequence stalls, and end-to-end perf bench harness + dashboards.

Key design points: single continuous string description: buckets are defined by configurable boundaries (default: [1-32,33-64,65-128,129-256,257+]) and an adaptive merge policy merges adjacent buckets when fill-rate falls below target to avoid underutilized device lanes; allocator computes estimated padded_tokens and estimated latency delta for candidate groupings and only applies splitting when padding reduction yields >X% token savings or predicted latency impact is within SLO budget. The kernel-selection table was extended to record median_seqlen histograms per model/variant.

Testing and results: microbenchmarks on T4 and A100 show 8-18% token-cost reduction and 6-12% p95 latency improvement for mixed-traffic workloads (chat-style + long-doc ingestion). Stress tests validated that KV cache correctness and continuity is preserved when splitting/grouping requests (no cache misses introduced). E2E perf pipeline added to nightly bench lab and tracked via the perf-canary dashboards.

Compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.dynamic_batching.seqlen_bucketing (default off for existing clusters). Gradual rollout plan: enable in canary region, collect metrics for 48h, then ramp across Dedicated pools. Tuning knobs exposed in console for bucket boundaries, merge thresholds, and padding-savings target.

Related: ENG-2891 (experimentation and perf sheets), ENG-2910 (scheduler preemption work), perf-canary lab runs linked in PR comments.

release_notes: Improved dynamic batching by grouping requests by sequence-length buckets and introducing a padding-minimization allocator. Expected benefits: lower padded token count, reduced per-token cost, and improved p95 latency for mixed-length workloads. Feature gated; rollout and tuning knobs available in the Console.
